LESTER, SUSAN, M.D.~PH.D. 
DIAGNOSIS: by LESTER,SUSAN,M.D.,PH.D. 
LEFT BREAST, MODIFIED RADICAL MASTECTOMY (509 GRAMS): 
DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU, solid type, present adjacent to biopsy site 
(largest focus 0.8cm ). 
Inked resection margins are free of tumor. 
No invasive tumor seen. 
Fibrocystic changes. 
No tumor present in sixteen (16) axillary lymph nodes. 
Note: A single suspicious cluster of cells was present in one lymph node. 
Immunohistochemical studies on the same slide (after removal of the coverslip) 
revealed that the cells were not immunoreactive for keratin ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID / REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) and, 
therefore, do NOT represent a metastatic focus. 
RIGHT BREAST, RE-EXCISION: 
DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU, solid type (intermediate grade nuclear features) 
(present in two of seventeen slides). In situ carcinoma is 0.2cm from 
the margin in both blocks and is found adjacent to the biopsy site and 
about 1cm from the biopsy site. 
Fibrocystic changes. 
No invasive tumor seen. 
CLINICAL DATA: 
History: None given. 
Operation: Right quadrantectomy, left MRM, and latissiimus dorsai flap and 
implant. 
Clinical Diagnosis: Bilateral breast cancer. 
TISSUE SUBMITTED: 1. Right breast quadrantectomy (long-anterior, medial; 
short-anterior, lateral). 
2. Left breast plus axillary nodes. 
GROSS DESCRIPTION: by BRIMHALL,BRADLEY BASEL,M.D. 
The specimen is received fresh as two (2) parts. 
The first, labeled "left breast and axillary nodes", consists of 509 gram 
modified radical mastectomy specimen, measuring 21 x REMOVED_DATE x 3cm  Overlying 
the specimen is a triangular shaped skin fragment measuring 9.5cm on one side, 
6.5cm on another, and 8cm on the third side. The 6.5cm side is facing 
laterally. Adjacent to the 6.5cm side, there is a 5.1cm long, well-healed 
scar. The areolar measures 3.3cm  and the nipple measures 0.9cm and is 
inverted. Approximately 1.1cm deep to the scar site is a 4 x 3 x 2.5cm 
hemorrhagic biopsy cavity surrounded by firm, fibrous tissue and fat necrosis. 
The remainder of the breast is finely nodular with numerous blue-dome cysts, 
suggestive of fibrocystic changes. The axillary tail measures 7 x 7 x 2.5cm 
and contains thirteen (13) possible lymph nodes. There are no other discreet 
lesions, aside from the biopsy cavity, within the breast parenchyma.
